findings.title: Duplicates monthly price logic instead of reusing monthlyPriceMinor
findings.explanation: The file already has `monthlyPriceMinor(plan, currency, seats)`, which returns minor units. The new function re-reads `PLANS[plan].monthly[currency] * seats` directly and bypasses it. Any logic in the existing function (seat tiers, minimums, per-currency handling) is silently skipped. The PR's goal is for checkout and invoicing to compute prices the same way, and this breaks that. Build on `monthlyPriceMinor(...)` so the two prices cannot drift apart.

findings.title: Hardcoded `* 100` gives wrong amounts for non-2-decimal currencies
findings.explanation: Multiplying by 100 assumes every currency has two minor-unit decimals. Zero-decimal currencies (JPY, KRW) and three-decimal ones (KWD, BHD) would be invoiced at the wrong amount, by 100x or 10x. Use the same currency-exponent handling as `monthlyPriceMinor`, or derive it from the currency. Add a test for at least one currency that is not 2-decimal.

findings.title: Floating-point arithmetic on money
findings.explanation: `monthly * 12 * 0.9 * 100` mixes binary floats (0.9 is not exactly representable, and major-unit prices like 9.99 are not either). The result can land just below or above a .5 boundary, so `Math.round` can be off by one minor unit. The checkout and invoice totals could then disagree with each other or with the payment provider. Do the math in integer minor units, for example `Math.round(monthlyMinor * seats * 108 / 10)`, or use a decimal library. Define the rounding rule explicitly (half-up, per invoice versus per seat) and keep it in one place.

findings.title: No tests for the new pricing function
findings.explanation: This function determines what customers are charged. Add unit tests covering each plan and currency, a 1-seat case and a many-seat case, rounding edge cases (amounts ending in .5 minor units), and zero-decimal currencies. Also assert consistency with `monthlyPriceMinor * 12 * 0.9` to guard against drift.

findings.title: No validation of `seats`
findings.explanation: Non-integer, zero, negative or NaN seat counts flow straight into the amount and could produce zero, negative or fractional invoices. Validate that `seats` is a positive integer here or at the callers, consistent with what `monthlyPriceMinor` does.

findings.title: Magic numbers for months and discount
findings.explanation: `12` and `0.9` are inline. Extract named constants such as `ANNUAL_MONTHS = 12` and `ANNUAL_DISCOUNT_PERCENT = 10`, so the discount can be changed in one place and is easy to find when the product team adjusts it.

prompt:
Review this pull request.

## Add annual plan pricing

Annual billing launches next month: twelve months for the price of 10.8 (a 10% discount). Adds `annualPriceMinor` next to the monthly price so the checkout page and the invoice generator compute it the same way.

## Diff

```diff
diff --git a/src/services/pricing.ts b/src/services/pricing.ts
index 142a18d..f738804 100644
--- a/src/services/pricing.ts
+++ b/src/services/pricing.ts
@@ -16,3 +16,9 @@ export function monthlyPriceMinor(plan: Plan, currency: Currency, seats: number)
 export function planLabel(plan: Plan): string {
   return plan === 'team' ? 'Team' : 'Business'
 }
+
+// Annual billing: twelve months with a 10% discount, in minor units for the invoice.
+export function annualPriceMinor(plan: Plan, currency: Currency, seats: number): number {
+  const monthly = PLANS[plan].monthly[currency] * seats
+  return Math.round(monthly * 12 * 0.9 * 100)
+}
```
